habitat: Deep, clear fresh water, in pairs or flocks.
summary: A dark diving duck of deep fresh water. The male has a blue-grey bill, a uniform dark head and back, a crimson eye and a longer neck than Maccoa Duck. Newman describes him as entirely dark brown with a bronzy sheen. The female has a whitish crescent on the sides of the head and white on the throat and at the base of the bill. In flight a whitish speculum runs the full width of the wing. Newman says there is no distinctive call. The African birds are the race brunnea.

similar.note: Yellow-billed Duck has a yellow bill with a black patch and pale-edged feathers. A male Southern Pochard is more uniformly dark, with a blue-grey bill and a crimson eye.

viewNotes.note: Male: a uniform dark head, a crimson eye and a blue-grey bill. Female: a pale crescent on the side of the head.
The female crescent and white throat show from the front. The male face is uniformly dark, with a red eye.
The male back is uniformly dark. The female upperparts are the dark half of the pattern.
The whitish speculum runs the full width of the wing.
The underwing is not given a separate colour in these texts.
The male eye is crimson and the head and back are uniform.
The female has a whitish crescent on the side of the head and white at the bill base.

calls.description: Newman says there is no distinctive call. No playable recording was found: the catalogue files for this species are ND.

research.note: Months in Kruger are not listed. SABAP1 says it is thinly distributed and nomadic in the Transvaal and scarce in the northern Transvaal, with partial moult and other movements. A male photograph, chick down, juvenile plumage and a playable call were not found. Wikipedia did not add a usable plumage paragraph beyond the sexes already in Newman. Maccoa Duck is the comparison in Newman and is not on the Kruger list, so it is not linked. Status is omitted because SABAP1 describes regular seasonal movements as well as nomadism.
